verdict.rationale: The only on-topic evidence is GitHub's fine-grained personal access tokens. These let you grant a token a specific set of permissions that define which resources it can reach via the API, and the API reports the required permissions in a header. That is a narrow form of granular access control, scoped to API tokens rather than to people and teams across the org/project/repo/branch hierarchy. Missing for 10: organization/workspace-level role management, project-level permissions, repository collaborator/team roles, branch-level protection rules, and any independent corroboration.
